4.label: Exceeds Standard
4.description: Demonstrates deep understanding; solves complex, multi-step problems accurately; explains reasoning clearly.

3.label: Meets Standard
3.description: Consistently applies grade-level concepts correctly with minor errors; meets all CCSS expectations.

2.label: Approaching Standard
2.description: Partially applies concepts; makes procedural errors; inconsistent accuracy across question types.

1.label: Below Standard
1.description: Limited or no grasp of grade-level concepts; significant errors; unable to complete standard tasks independently.

standards.description: Use parentheses, brackets, or braces in numerical expressions, and evaluate expressions with these symbols.

levels.4: Correctly evaluates complex nested expressions with all three grouping symbols; explains order of operations at each step.
levels.3: Correctly evaluates expressions with parentheses and brackets using order of operations with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Evaluates expressions with parentheses correctly but makes errors with nested brackets or braces.
levels.1: Cannot correctly apply order of operations or grouping symbols.

standards.description: Write simple expressions that record calculations with numbers, and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them.

levels.4: Writes and interprets complex expressions fluently; explains the meaning of an expression in context without computing.
levels.3: Correctly writes and interprets numerical expressions for given verbal descriptions with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Writes expressions correctly but struggles to interpret them in words, or vice versa.
levels.1: Cannot write or interpret numerical expressions accurately.

standards.description: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules; identify relationships between corresponding terms; form and graph ordered pairs.

levels.4: Generates both patterns correctly; articulates the relationship between them; accurately forms and graphs all ordered pairs on a coordinate plane.
levels.3: Generates both patterns and identifies the relationship; graphs most ordered pairs correctly with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Generates one pattern correctly; struggles to identify the relationship or graph the ordered pairs.
levels.1: Cannot generate patterns from rules or form ordered pairs.

standards.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as in the place to its right and 1/10 as much as in the place to its left.

levels.4: Explains the 10× and 1/10 relationship across both whole number and decimal place values; connects to multiplication and division by powers of 10.
levels.3: Correctly identifies the relationship in both directions (10× right, 1/10 left) for whole numbers and decimals with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Understands the 10× relationship for whole numbers but inconsistent with decimal place values or the 1/10 direction.
levels.1: Cannot describe place value relationships in multi-digit or decimal numbers.

standards.description: Explain patterns in the number of zeros when multiplying by powers of 10; use whole-number exponents to denote powers of 10.

levels.4: Explains the pattern for both multiplication and division by powers of 10; uses exponent notation correctly; applies to decimal shifting.
levels.3: Correctly uses whole-number exponents for powers of 10 and explains the zero-pattern rule with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Applies the pattern for multiplication but makes errors with division or exponent notation.
levels.1: Cannot identify or apply patterns when multiplying or dividing by powers of 10.

standards.description: Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form.

levels.4: Reads, writes, and compares decimals to thousandths in all three forms fluently; places decimals precisely on a number line.
levels.3: Correctly reads, writes, and compares decimals to thousandths with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Reads and writes decimals correctly but makes errors in comparison or expanded form at the thousandths level.
levels.1: Significant errors reading, writing, or comparing decimals to thousandths.

standards.description: Use place value understanding to round decimals to any place.

levels.4: Rounds decimals accurately to any place; explains the decision process; applies rounding in real-world context problems.
levels.3: Rounds decimals to tenths and hundredths correctly with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Rounds whole numbers correctly but makes errors rounding to decimal places.
levels.1: Cannot reliably round decimals to any place.

standards.description: Fluently multiply multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

levels.4: Applies the standard algorithm fluently with zero errors; can identify errors in others' work and explain the algorithm conceptually.
levels.3: Correctly multiplies multi-digit numbers using the standard algorithm with ≤1 computational error.
levels.2: Uses the algorithm but makes regrouping or partial-product errors in ≥2 problems.
levels.1: Cannot apply the standard multiplication algorithm correctly.

standards.description: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors using strategies based on place value.

levels.4: Divides four-digit by two-digit numbers correctly using multiple strategies; interprets remainder in context; explains reasoning.
levels.3: Correctly finds quotients and remainders for four-digit ÷ two-digit problems with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Divides correctly with one-digit divisors; makes errors with two-digit divisors.
levels.1: Cannot reliably divide multi-digit numbers by two-digit divisors.

standards.description: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value.

levels.4: Performs all four decimal operations accurately to hundredths; explains strategy; connects to place value understanding.
levels.3: Correctly adds, subtracts, multiplies, and divides decimals to hundredths with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Correctly adds and subtracts decimals; makes errors multiplying or dividing decimals.
levels.1: Cannot reliably perform decimal operations to hundredths.

standards.description: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators by replacing given fractions with equivalent fractions.

levels.4: Adds and subtracts fractions and mixed numbers with unlike denominators fluently; simplifies results; explains the equivalence strategy.
levels.3: Correctly adds and subtracts fractions with unlike denominators; finds LCD with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Adds/subtracts when one denominator is a multiple of the other; errors with unrelated denominators.
levels.1: Cannot add or subtract fractions with unlike denominators.

standards.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions with unlike denominators; use benchmark fractions to estimate.

levels.4: Solves multi-step fraction word problems accurately; uses benchmark fractions to check reasonableness; explains solution.
levels.3: Correctly sets up and solves fraction addition/subtraction word problems with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Sets up problem correctly but makes computational errors; limited use of estimation.
levels.1: Cannot set up or solve fraction word problems with unlike denominators.

standards.description: Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator; solve word problems involving division of whole numbers leading to fractions or mixed numbers.

levels.4: Interprets fractions as division in multiple contexts; solves and explains problems where whole-number division yields a fraction or mixed number.
levels.3: Correctly interprets a/b as a ÷ b and solves related word problems with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Understands the concept in simple cases but struggles to apply in word problem contexts.
levels.1: Cannot interpret a fraction as division or apply it to problem solving.

standards.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction; find the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths.

levels.4: Multiplies fractions and mixed numbers correctly; finds area of rectangles with fractional sides; connects to area model; explains scaling.
levels.3: Correctly multiplies a fraction by a fraction and a fraction by a whole number with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Multiplies simple fractions correctly; errors with mixed numbers or area model application.
levels.1: Cannot multiply fractions correctly.

standards.description: Interpret multiplication as scaling (resizing); compare the size of a product to the size of one factor without performing multiplication.

levels.4: Explains scaling for fractions greater than 1, equal to 1, and less than 1; predicts and justifies product size without computing.
levels.3: Correctly identifies whether a product is larger or smaller than a factor based on the multiplier with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Understands scaling for whole numbers but inconsistent with fractional multipliers less than 1.
levels.1: Cannot interpret multiplication as scaling or compare product and factor sizes.

standards.description: Solve real-world problems involving multiplication of fractions and mixed numbers.

levels.4: Solves multi-step real-world problems involving fractions and mixed numbers; labels units; checks reasonableness.
levels.3: Correctly solves fraction multiplication word problems with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Solves problems with unit fractions or simple proper fractions; errors with mixed numbers.
levels.1: Cannot set up or solve real-world fraction multiplication problems.

standards.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of division to divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions.

levels.4: Divides unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions accurately; creates and solves related word problems; explains with visual models.
levels.3: Correctly divides in both directions (unit fraction ÷ whole number and whole number ÷ unit fraction) with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Divides correctly in one direction; errors in the other, or cannot apply to word problems.
levels.1: Cannot divide involving unit fractions.

standards.description: Convert among different-sized standard measurement units within a given measurement system.

levels.4: Converts fluently within and between metric and customary systems; applies multi-step conversions in context.
levels.3: Correctly converts within a measurement system across common units with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Converts simple, frequently practiced pairs; errors on multi-step or less familiar conversions.
levels.1: Cannot reliably convert between measurement units.

standards.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit; use operations on fractions to solve problems.

levels.4: Creates an accurate line plot with fractional units; solves multi-step addition/subtraction problems from the data.
levels.3: Creates a correct line plot and answers fraction-based questions about the data with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Creates line plot with minor errors; answers basic reading questions but not multi-step analysis.
levels.1: Cannot create or interpret a line plot with fractional measurement data.

standards.description: Recognize volume as an attribute of solid figures; understand that a unit cube has 1 cubic unit of volume.

levels.4: Explains volume as the number of unit cubes needed to fill a solid; applies concept to non-rectangular prisms by decomposition.
levels.3: Correctly identifies volume as the count of unit cubes and applies the concept to standard figures.
levels.2: Understands the concept of volume but confuses it with area or surface area in some cases.
levels.1: Cannot explain or apply the concept of volume as counting unit cubes.

standards.description: Measure volumes by counting unit cubes, using cubic cm, cubic in, cubic ft, and improvised units.

levels.4: Counts unit cubes accurately for irregular arrangements; correctly labels units; estimates volume of real objects.
levels.3: Correctly counts unit cubes to find volume with ≤1 counting or labeling error.
levels.2: Counts visible unit cubes correctly but undercounts hidden layers; inconsistent labeling.
levels.1: Cannot correctly count unit cubes to determine volume.

standards.description: Relate volume to multiplication and addition; find volumes of right rectangular prisms using formulas V = l × w × h and V = B × h; find volumes of composite figures.

levels.4: Applies both volume formulas correctly; decomposes composite figures and adds volumes; explains the relationship between the formulas.
levels.3: Correctly calculates volume using V = l × w × h and V = B × h with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Applies one formula correctly but not both; struggles with composite figures.
levels.1: Cannot apply volume formulas correctly.

standards.description: Use a pair of perpendicular number lines (axes) to define a coordinate system; understand that the first number in an ordered pair indicates horizontal distance and the second indicates vertical distance.

levels.4: Correctly plots and reads points in all four quadrants of the coordinate plane; explains the meaning of each coordinate.
levels.3: Correctly plots and reads ordered pairs in the first quadrant with ≤1 error; labels axes.
levels.2: Plots points when given step-by-step guidance; reverses x and y coordinates in some cases.
levels.1: Cannot correctly plot or identify ordered pairs on a coordinate plane.

standards.description: Represent real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points in the first quadrant; interpret coordinate values in context.

levels.4: Graphs points accurately and interprets coordinate values in complex real-world contexts; connects to patterns and relationships.
levels.3: Correctly graphs points and interprets their meaning in context with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Graphs points correctly but struggles to interpret what the coordinates represent in context.
levels.1: Cannot graph points or interpret coordinate values in real-world problems.

standards.description: Understand that attributes belonging to a category of two-dimensional figures also belong to all subcategories.

levels.4: Accurately explains the hierarchy of 2D shapes; applies category attributes to all subcategories; provides examples and counterexamples.
levels.3: Correctly identifies that subcategory figures share all attributes of the parent category with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Understands some relationships (e.g., squares are rectangles) but cannot generalize across the full hierarchy.
levels.1: Cannot apply category attributes to subcategories of 2D figures.

standards.description: Classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy based on properties.

levels.4: Correctly places all 2D figures in a complete hierarchy; justifies placement using precise geometric properties; identifies overlapping categories.
levels.3: Correctly classifies 2D figures in a hierarchy using relevant properties with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Classifies common shapes correctly; errors with less familiar shapes or overlapping categories.
levels.1: Cannot classify 2D figures using a hierarchy of properties.
